about: Adam, Nov 17 2026: "yes!" to the 26 Coworker services P1 to P26, the Coworker + Adobe Analytics connection that P8 needs and the six RFI write-ups, as verified in the Coworker review (each service read on its Adobe page, checked by a second reader and its quote found word for word, live on Nov 17). This is that record, with the id each service took. CW09 to CW11 are Coworker's own services on the Services step (index.html CATALOG) and under More services on the Coworker card; the other 23 are research lines on their connections (canvas/research). A research line carries its name, hours, scope, quote and source, and the Services step treats it as a service concept the partner writes up, so the deliverable, acceptance, assumptions and exclusions below are kept here for that. In CW09 to CW11 a service named by its id is named by its name instead, since partners never see internal ids. CW10's assumptions also say "the Client" where the text below says "the customer", the word the statement of work always uses for the client. Coworker Chat on Adobe Analytics report suites (P8) was proposed on by default; it starts off so saved canvases keep their totals. Hours are our own estimates; Adobe publishes none.

services.name: Coworker governance and access policy
services.attach_to: [P1] Coworker product (cw), under More services. Services page stage: Launch; play: coworker.
services.scope: Define how the Client runs Coworker beyond the pilot, for up to three teams: the organization-wide access setting and the user and group overrides, Coworker user groups for the agreed teams, the roles those groups hold in the connected applications, which task types must use Plan mode and who approves them, which actions are allowed in which sandbox (including deletes and moving objects between sandboxes), whether users may add their own servers and install or remove plugins, the memory rules, the audit review routine and an AI credit plan for the agreed use cases.
services.deliverable: Coworker operating policy, access model with user groups and overrides, action and approval rules by application and sandbox, server and plugin rules for users, memory and audit routines, AI credit plan, and joiner and leaver steps.
services.acceptance: The Client's administrators and governance owner approve the policy, the agreed groups and overrides are in place, and tests show users reach only what their application roles allow.
services.assumptions: Coworker is provisioned and the pilot is accepted or under way. A Coworker administrator (a System Admin, or a Product Admin of Experience Platform) applies the settings. Where Adobe's onboarding team has already defined governance and approval workflows, this service builds on that work. Coworker user groups are separate from Admin Console groups and are kept in Coworker. AI credit rates are Adobe's and can change.
services.exclusions: Pilot access and context validation already in CW02, broad permission cleanup in the connected applications, sandbox and data usage policy setup (RT05), Adobe-owned provisioning and ongoing administration.
services.quote: Onboarding: Adobe’s enterprise support or professional services team configures Coworker for your environment, sets up integrations with your Adobe applications, and defines governance and approval workflows.
services.why_distinct: CW02 validates two permission paths and one context pack for the pilot and excludes broad access work, and CW07 builds the marketplace but leaves the decision on who may install plugins to administrators. Nothing in the tool prices the organization-wide access model, Coworker user groups, Plan mode and action rules by sandbox, server and plugin rules, memory and audit routines or the credit plan that a wider rollout needs. Supporting pages: coworker/content/administration/access-control (organization-wide setting plus user or group overrides; Coworker user groups are separate from Admin Console groups), coworker/content/chat/ui-guide (Plan mode for tasks that change data), coworker/content/customizations/plugins/manage-plugins-for-your-org (whether users can install or remove plugins themselves), coworker/content/customizations/memory/what-is-memory, cx-enterprise-ai/experience-cloud-ai/overview/ai-credit-consumption.
services.review: Corrected in review: adds the rules on whether users may add servers and install or remove plugins. Step 86: the sentence on Adobe's progressive rollout of Access control and Audit is out of the assumptions; the fact is in the notes.

bands.small: 1 team, organization default and overrides, action rules for 1 application
bands.typical: Up to 3 teams, the agreed applications and sandboxes, 1 AI credit plan
bands.large: Up to 6 teams, 5 applications and several sandboxes

services.name: Custom MCP server for a Client system
services.attach_to: [P2] Coworker product (cw), under More services. Services page stage: Connect; play: coworker.
services.scope: Design, build and host one MCP server that gives Coworker governed access to a Client system with no built-in connector, such as an internal API, a product catalog or a ticketing tool: up to six tools, read-only by default with any write tools behind confirmation, the authentication method and headers Coworker sends, and the tool timeout. Register it in Coworker as a server, test each tool with authorized and unauthorized users, and document who may add servers.
services.deliverable: The MCP server code and hosting setup, its tool list with read and write scope, the Coworker server registration, security and test evidence, and run and removal instructions.
services.acceptance: Authorized users complete the agreed tasks through the new tools in Coworker, unauthorized requests are refused, and the Client's security owner approves the server.
services.assumptions: The Client provides the system's API documentation, a test environment, credentials and a hosting location it owns. The Client's security team reviews the integration, since connecting an MCP server to Adobe products is a configuration the customer chooses and must evaluate. Coworker reaches the server over SSE or HTTP at the URL it is given. In Coworker, each user adds servers on the Integrations tab of their Customizations, so pilot users add it there unless the Client's administrators share it in a plugin, which is priced in CW07.
services.exclusions: Changes to the Client's system or API, more than one system, ongoing hosting and support, Adobe's built-in connectors (CW04) and plugin packaging (CW07).
services.quote: MCP connectors: Act across Adobe and external systems through governed access, using built-in connectors or your own.
services.why_distinct: CW04 and CW07 both exclude new MCP servers, so no service builds one. Adobe names your own connectors as a Coworker building block, and the Coworker Chat guide (coworker/content/chat/ui-guide, Connect a server) documents adding a server by URL with its connection type, tool timeout, authentication and headers. developer.adobe.com/analytics-mcp/docs/ adds that customers are responsible for evaluating the security and suitability of any MCP integration.
services.review: Corrected in review: says where servers are added and points sharing to a plugin (CW07). Wording: names the Integrations tab instead of saying Adobe has servers added.

bands.small: 3 read-only tools on one API with key-based authentication
bands.typical: 1 MCP server for 1 system, up to 6 tools

services.name: Coworker trial value sprint
services.attach_to: [P3] Coworker product (cw), under More services. Services page stage: Launch; play: coworker.
services.scope: For a Client that Adobe has accepted into the usage-bound Coworker trial, choose up to three use cases with the business owners, prepare the data access and example prompts, run them with up to 10 pilot users within the trial's AI credits, track use on the license usage dashboard, and report the time saved, the quality of results and the open issues for the Client's purchase decision.
services.deliverable: Use case briefs, a credit budget for each use case, run logs with example results, and a value report with recommendations for a paid rollout.
services.acceptance: The Client's sponsor accepts the value report, and each use case shows its measured result against the agreed success measure.
services.assumptions: Adobe decides trial eligibility, and the trial is not open to customers who have or had a license to Experience Platform Agents AI Credits. The trial gives a one-time allotment of up to 10,000 AI credits and ends when they are used or the Client buys more. For a limited introductory period each Coworker input uses 25 AI credits, about 400 inputs for the whole trial; Adobe can change the rate. Users act only within their existing product permissions. Pilot users are a training scope, not a seat limit.
services.exclusions: Skill building (CW03), connections (CW04), what Adobe enables for the trial, the paid rollout and any license or credit purchase.
services.quote: Certain eligible CX Enterprise customers may have access to a usage-bound trial to experience the value of Adobe’s agentic AI offerings in their own environment before making the commitment to purchase.
services.why_distinct: CW01 plans workflows and CW05 pilots workflows whose Skills have passed testing. Nothing in the tool prices a credit-bounded run that proves value before purchase, which is how Adobe positions the trial.
services.review: Corrected in review: adds that the trial is not open to customers who have or had Experience Platform Agents AI Credits. Step 86: the sentence on Adobe's rolling move from AI Assistant to Coworker Chat is out of the assumptions; the fact is in the notes.

bands.typical: Up to 3 use cases, up to 10 pilot users

services.name: Implementation plan from Coworker, checked against the tenant
services.attach_to: [P4] Connection cw-cja (Coworker and Customer Journey Analytics), under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Run Coworker's implementation guide skill with your client's team for one path (Customer Journey Analytics from scratch, the Adobe Analytics upgrade, Content Analytics, Marketing Campaign Analytics or Streaming Media), check each planned step against the live tenant (licenses, sandboxes, schemas, datasets, report suites and permissions), correct the owners and effort, and import the plan into Workfront or Jira as the delivery plan.
services.deliverable: The checked plan with owners, effort and dependencies, the list of steps the tenant check changed, and the Workfront or Jira import.
services.acceptance: Your client's project owner approves the plan, and every step names an owner and the service that delivers it.
services.assumptions: Your client has Coworker Chat and access to the product being planned. The skill only plans: it does not read the tenant or make changes, so the tenant check is done by people with the right access. CJ03 already includes planning the upgrade path and CA01 covers the Content Analytics prerequisites, so when either is also selected this plan replaces that planning work and their hours are reduced rather than charged twice.
services.exclusions: Delivering the implementation (priced in each product's own services), Coworker Projects and ongoing project management.
services.quote: These skills don’t access your Adobe systems or make any changes. They help you plan your implementation. They don’t perform it or verify it against a live tenant.
services.why_distinct: Only CJ03 (its upgrade plan) and CA01 (Content Analytics prerequisites) touch planning, and neither checks a generated plan against the live tenant or loads it into Workfront or Jira. The checked plan feeds CJ01 to CJ03, XL07 and XL08, CA01 and CA02, MM01 to MM03, and the Streaming Media service P7. Adobe lists the next stage, an implementation checklist in Coworker Projects, as Experimental (coworker/content/chat/use-cases/data-insights/intelligent-implementation-and-administration/data-governance-and-validation), so it stays excluded.
services.review: Corrected in review: now a clear inference, and an assumption keeps CJ03 or CA01 planning from being charged twice. Step 86: the release label after Coworker Projects is gone; the exclusion stays.

services.name: Adobe Analytics and CJA data validation and fixes
services.attach_to: [P5] Connection cw-cja, under More services (default: false), with needs: ["aa"] so it shows only when Adobe Analytics is also on the canvas.
services.scope: After your client completes the upgrade steps, run Coworker's validation skill on up to three report suite and data view pairs (a full audit compares up to 40 metrics and 20 dimensions), check each suggested action, and fix the causes in Experience Platform, Adobe Analytics or the data view, such as bot filtering, session settings, marketing channel derived fields, duplicate datasets or field mappings. Rerun until each pair reaches the agreed matching rate, and document the differences that are expected by design, such as device-based visitors against people.
services.deliverable: Validation results before and after, the fix log, the list of expected differences for stakeholders, and a sign-off record for relying on CJA.
services.acceptance: Each agreed pair reaches the agreed matching rate, for example Good (90% or more) on Adobe's scale, or every remaining gap is explained and accepted by your client's analytics owner.
services.assumptions: Users running the skill can view both the report suite and the data view. The upgrade steps are complete (CJ03, XL07 or another statement of work), since validation follows all previous upgrade steps. Some variance is expected and is documented rather than forced to zero.
services.exclusions: The upgrade itself, project and component migration (XL08), new data collection, and sources other than Adobe Analytics and CJA.
services.quote: Verify that the suggested actions are valid, then resolve them in Adobe Experience Platform or Adobe Analytics.
services.why_distinct: CJ03 and XL07 price the upgrade and the report suite data in CJA. Nothing prices the reconciliation sprint: Coworker's skill flags differences and suggests fixes, and the aa-cja-validation skill lists resolving the underlying cause of a data discrepancy as out of scope (coworker/content/chat/use-cases/data-insights/analytics-overview, Skills and limitations).
services.review: Corrected in review: validation starts once the upgrade steps are complete, and the out-of-scope point cites the analytics overview. Wording: drops the Adobe says framing.

services.name: Coworker analytics enablement on CJA data views
services.attach_to: [P6] Connection cw-cja, under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Set up the organization-level practices Adobe recommends for analysis in Coworker, for up to two teams: coach an analyst from your client's team as the Coworker champion, agree the approved dimensions, metrics and segments in each data view and tidy their names and descriptions so prompts can name them exactly, write a library of up to 20 vetted prompts and one Skill that directs Coworker to the approved components, store each team's data view in memory, and teach users when to ask for a quick answer and when to work through a deeper analysis.
services.deliverable: The approved component list for each data view, the vetted prompt library, the component Skill with test evidence, memory preferences and a short user guide.
services.acceptance: Pilot users get answers built from the approved components for each prompt in the library, and your client's champion approves the library and the Skill.
services.assumptions: Data views exist and hold the agreed components, and users can open them in Analysis Workspace, since Coworker inherits those permissions. Coworker does not create or edit data view components, so component changes are made in CJA by people with that access. Organization-level skill libraries need an administrator's setup, and a saved skill is not shared with other users automatically, so the Skill reaches the teams through an administrator's skill library or a plugin (CW07).
services.exclusions: New data views or components (CJ02), other Skills (CW03) and the AI-channel readout Skills (CW-CJA), pilot training (CW05), monthly prompt upkeep (CW06) and the in-product Coworker panel in Workspace.
services.quote: Create a library of vetted prompts and skills that correlate with the data and components that are available to users.
services.why_distinct: CW-CJA builds two Skills for an AI-channel readout and CW06 maintains prompts each month. No service sets up the champion, the vetted library tied to the Client's own components and the component Skill, which Adobe lists as organization-level best practices.
services.review: Corrected in review: adds how the Skill reaches the teams (an administrator's skill library or a plugin). Step 86: the release label after the Workspace panel is gone; the exclusion stays.

services.name: Streaming Media collection from the Coworker plan
services.attach_to: [P7] Connection cw-cja, under More services (default: false). It could instead sit on the CJA or Adobe Analytics product if Adam wants it to show without Coworker.
services.scope: Instrument your client's video or audio players for Streaming Media collection on the Edge, from the plan Coworker's implementation guide skill produces: configure the datastream and the XDM schema and dataset for media events, implement the SDK or API on up to two player platforms, map the media event model, add the media components to the CJA data view where CJA reports, and check that sessions, pings and completions reach CJA or Adobe Analytics reporting.
services.deliverable: The configured datastream, schema and dataset, the player implementation on each agreed platform, the event mapping, the data view components where CJA reports, test evidence and a reporting check.
services.acceptance: Test sessions on each agreed platform show the expected starts, pings and completions in your client's CJA or Adobe Analytics reports.
services.assumptions: Your client's CJA or Adobe Analytics package covers Streaming Media collection, and your client owns the player code and gives developers access to it. The plan comes from P4 or your client's own run of the skill.
services.exclusions: Player development beyond the tracking calls, more than two platforms, chapter and ad tracking unless agreed, reports beyond the reporting check, and Coworker's Streaming Media Validation skill.
services.quote: Get an implementation plan for Streaming Media collection on the Edge, covering datastream configuration, per-platform SDK/API implementation, and the media event model, so you correctly instrument sessions, pings, and completions for Customer Journey Analytics and/or Adobe Analytics reporting.
services.why_distinct: No service in the tool prices Streaming Media collection. Coworker's guide plans it, and the same page says the skills do not perform or verify the implementation. Adobe lists the Coworker Streaming Media validation use case as Experimental (coworker/content/chat/use-cases/data-insights/intelligent-implementation-and-administration/data-governance-and-validation), so the reporting check is done in CJA or Adobe Analytics, not with that skill.
services.review: Corrected in review: adds the schema, dataset and data view steps and excludes Coworker's Streaming Media validation skill. Step 86: that skill's release label is gone, and the package line reads as what the client must own instead of a check with Adobe.

services.name: Coworker Chat on Adobe Analytics report suites
services.attach_to: [P8] Needs a new connection that Adobe documents: cw-aa (Coworker and Adobe Analytics). The Coworker overview lists Adobe Analytics among the applications where Coworker Chat is available now, and the Adobe Analytics release notes give Coworker Chat analysis of report suites general availability on October 29, 2026. Default: on (like XH01 on ca-cw).
services.scope: Give your client's pilot users Adobe Analytics MCP access in their product profiles (MCP Read-only Access for analysis, or MCP Full Access where they may also create segments, calculated metrics or projects), check that the aa-mcp integration is connected in Coworker, agree the report suite each team uses and store it in memory, compare the first answers with Analysis Workspace, and write the starter prompts and one Skill that keeps Coworker on the approved components, including root cause questions about a known metric over a known period.
services.deliverable: Permission and integration check, memory preferences, a prompt set with Workspace comparisons, one tested component Skill and a short user guide.
services.acceptance: Pilot users get answers that match Workspace for the agreed reports, using only the report suites and components they can see.
services.assumptions: Your client licenses Adobe Analytics and Coworker. Coworker inherits each user's Adobe Analytics permissions, and Adobe Analytics product administrators get full MCP access automatically. Organization-level skill libraries need an administrator's setup, so the Skill reaches the team through one or through a plugin (CW07).
services.exclusions: Report suite and component builds (AN02, AN04), the Adobe Analytics to CJA validation (P5) and project migration (XL08).
services.quote: Select the Integrations tab, then make sure that cja-mcp and aa-mcp are available in your list of connected servers.
services.why_distinct: The tool has no Coworker and Adobe Analytics connection, so nothing prices this setup; XH01 does the same job for Content Analytics. Supporting pages: developer.adobe.com/analytics-mcp/docs/guides/permissions (MCP Read-only Access and MCP Full Access; product administrators get full MCP access automatically), analytics/release-notes/latest (Coworker Chat analysis of report suites generally available October 29, 2026; MCP Access renamed MCP Full Access, October 6, 2026), coworker/content/chat/use-cases/data-insights/intelligent-implementation-and-administration/migrate-projects-aa-cja (Adobe Analytics MCP access as a Coworker prerequisite), coworker/content/chat/use-cases/data-insights/business-performance/root-cause-analysis.
services.review: Corrected in review: today's MCP permission names, product administrators' automatic access, Adobe's full sentence as the quote and a Skill sharing note. Step 86: the coming soon conflict and the confirm with Adobe sentence are out of the assumptions (the tool check would fail on both); attach_to and the notes keep them for Adam.
services.starts: off, so saved canvases keep their totals

services.name: Experience Platform health check fixes with Coworker
services.attach_to: [P9] Connection cw-rtcdp (Coworker and Real-Time CDP), under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Start from Coworker's view of the latest health check results for up to two of your client's sandboxes, let Coworker fix the issue types it supports after your client approves each change (identity namespace descriptions, duplicate and default merge policy names, and schemas missing the audit field group), and fix the other failed checks by hand, such as schema and identity configuration, TTL and lookback settings, segmentation and dataset limits, destination schedules, failing scheduled queries and source credentials. Add descriptions to the XDM fields teams target on so Coworker's field discovery finds them, rerun the checks and hand over a prioritized list of what is left.
services.deliverable: Health check results before and after, the change log for each fix, the field descriptions added, and the prioritized list of open issues with owners.
services.acceptance: The agreed failed checks pass on the next daily scan, and your client's platform owner approves the remaining list.
services.assumptions: Users have the View Health Checks permission and the Experience Platform permissions each fix needs. Fixes that change identity linking or merge behavior are tried in a development sandbox first. Data lake retention decisions are priced in P10.
services.exclusions: A redesign of the data model or identity strategy (RT01), new ingestion, retention policy decisions (P10) and monthly monitoring (P11).
services.quote: These issues are difficult to detect and often require specialized expertise to diagnose.
services.why_distinct: RT01 to RT06 design and run a new platform. No service fixes an existing sandbox's health check failures, and Coworker can fix only four issue types itself (coworker/content/chat/use-cases/workflows, Remediate health check issues).
services.review: Kept as written.

services.name: Data lake retention review with Coworker
services.attach_to: [P10] Connection cw-rtcdp, under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Use Coworker's Data Management Agent to list your client's large, unused or forgotten Experience Event datasets in up to two sandboxes, check how actively each is used and model the effect of a retention period, then review up to 15 shortlisted datasets with the data owners against business and legal retention needs, choose another data lifecycle tool where a whole dataset or another store must be cleaned, and apply the approved retention policies after Coworker's impact preview.
services.deliverable: The dataset shortlist with usage and impact evidence, the retention decisions signed by the data owners, and the applied policies with their audit log entries.
services.acceptance: Each approved policy shows in the dataset's settings and audit log, and the data owners have signed every decision.
services.assumptions: Users have access to the Data Management Agent and the Experience Platform permissions for the datasets and retention actions, and the Adobe CXO plugin is installed in Coworker (CW04 where it is not). The minimum retention period is 30 days, and expired data is removed by Adobe's scheduled jobs, not at once. Adobe's usage signals may not cover every factor, so each decision uses your client's business context.
services.exclusions: Carrying out whole-dataset deletions or other data lifecycle work beyond choosing the right tool, legal advice on retention periods, and monthly reviews.
services.quote: We recommend reviewing the available details and applying your business context before taking action.
services.why_distinct: No service reviews existing datasets for retention; RT05 and RT06 cover governance setup and monthly dataflows. Adobe states the Data Management Agent is available to all customers with access to Coworker (cx-enterprise-ai/experience-cloud-ai/agents/data-management).
services.review: Corrected in review: adds the Adobe CXO plugin as a prerequisite. Wording: drops the Adobe lists framing.

services.name: Monthly data quality checks with Coworker
services.attach_to: [P11] Connection cw-rtcdp, under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Each month, run Coworker's Data Validation skill on up to 10 of your client's critical datasets and their key identity and event fields, check streaming capacity and breaches for the agreed sandboxes, follow up flagged values with Query Service where a sample is not enough, log regressions with their cause, and agree fixes to mappings or source data with the data owners.
services.deliverable: A monthly data quality log with results by dataset and field, capacity status, regressions found and fixed, and open actions with owners.
services.acceptance: Each month's checks run on the agreed datasets, every regression has an owner and a fix date, and fixed fields pass on the next run.
services.assumptions: The skill reads a sample of about the most recent 1,000 rows and up to five fields per request, and does not change data, schemas or mappings. Fixes run through your client's change control; large fixes are priced separately. After three months, review the volume with your client and resize the band.
services.exclusions: Dataflow, destination and audience operations (RT06), health check fixes (P9), full-dataset audits beyond the agreed Query Service checks, and new ingestion.
services.quote: Run ongoing data stewardship checks on critical datasets to catch regressions early.
services.why_distinct: RT06 reviews dataflows, alerts and audiences each month. No service checks the values inside critical datasets, which Adobe positions the Data Validation skill for; the same page tells users to supplement it with Query Service or Data Prep where checks need more.
services.review: Kept as written.

services.name: Journeys built with Coworker: readiness, finishing and checks
services.attach_to: [P12] Connection cw-ajo (Coworker and Journey Optimizer), under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Prepare your client's team to build journeys with Coworker's Journey Create skill: give practitioners the Manage Journeys, View Journey Events, Data Sources and Actions, View Segments and Manage Segments permissions and keep others read-only, confirm the audiences, events and data sources exist, name custom actions so prompts can call them exactly, and pilot up to five journeys from prompts or flowchart images. Finish in the journey canvas what Journey Create does not set, such as A/B tests, dataset lookups, wave sending, schedule recurrence, audience namespaces and custom action field mapping, then check each expression, run Coworker's quick simulation and a manual simulation or test mode, and publish.
services.deliverable: Role setup record, readiness checklist, a prompt guide for journey requests, up to five finished and tested journeys, and the pre-publish checklist.
services.acceptance: Each pilot journey passes the agreed simulation and test cases before publishing, and your client's journey owner approves the checklist.
services.assumptions: Journey events, data sources and custom actions are configured (JO02), and audiences exist and are segmented (RT04). Quick simulation does not replace manual simulation, so complex journeys get manual test cases.
services.exclusions: Journey strategy, journeys built by hand without Coworker (JO05), content production, Channel Content Create and Skills (XA26).
services.quote: Make sure to check and validate any expressions that Journey Skills create to ensure that the correct fields and values are used.
services.why_distinct: XA26 writes Skills and JO05 builds journeys by hand. No service prices the permissions, readiness, canvas finishing and checks that Coworker-built journeys need; Adobe lists the features Journey Create does not support and says Quick Simulation does not fully replace manual simulation.
services.review: Kept in review. Step 86: the release label after Channel Content Create is gone (the tool check would fail on it); the exclusion stays.

services.name: Journey inventory and channel setup cleanup with Coworker
services.attach_to: [P13] Connection cw-ajo, under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Run Coworker's journey hygiene, custom action error and channel configuration checks on one of your client's sandboxes, then clean up what they find: rename journeys, actions and events with missing, generic or similar names, close old live journeys to new entrances, delete the stale drafts and finished journeys your client no longer needs, move what stays into folders with tags, split oversized journeys, fix the endpoints, authentication or payloads behind failing custom actions, and correct sender, reply-to, subdomain, IP pool and unsubscribe settings in Journey Optimizer, since Channel Operation only reads them.
services.deliverable: Hygiene and channel findings before and after, the change log, naming rules for journeys, actions and events, and open items with owners.
services.acceptance: A rerun of the hygiene and channel checks shows the agreed items fixed, and your client's Journey Optimizer owner approves the remaining list.
services.assumptions: Users have the View Journeys and Manage Journeys permissions and access to the channel configurations. Changes to live journeys go through new versions and your client's approval. The journey list offers delete, folders and tags rather than an archive, and Adobe does not allow deleting a closed or stopped journey, so long-closed journeys stay in the list until they finish.
services.exclusions: Monthly journey operations (JO06), new journeys, new channel setup (JO01) and deliverability work such as IP warmup (JO03).
services.quote: Get recommendations to clean up and stabilize your journey inventory.
services.why_distinct: JO06 reviews reports and fixes errors month by month. Nothing prices a one-time cleanup of an existing journey inventory and channel setup, which Coworker audits but cannot change (journey-optimizer/using/channels/channels-coworker-skills: Channel Operation is read-only). Journey list actions and the rule that only finished journeys can be deleted: journey-optimizer/using/orchestrate-journeys/manage-journey/journey-ui and manage-journey/end-journey.
services.review: Corrected in review: the journey list offers delete, folders and tags but no archive, and only finished journeys can be deleted.

services.name: Custom outbound channel with Channel Builder
services.attach_to: [P14] Connection cw-ajo, under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Connect one messaging service your client uses that Journey Optimizer does not support natively (for example WeChat, Kakao Talk or a proprietary SMS gateway) to Journey Optimizer as a custom channel with Coworker's Channel Builder skill: the endpoint, headers and authentication, the throttling policy and the message payload. Test each payload scenario while the channel is still a draft, activate it, set up its API credentials where it uses authentication, its channel configuration and, where link tracking is needed, a delegated subdomain, and use it in a first journey or campaign.
services.deliverable: The active custom channel with its API credentials and channel configuration, its configuration record, payload test results and a first journey or campaign that uses it.
services.acceptance: Test messages reach the provider for each agreed payload scenario, and the channel sends from a live journey or campaign.
services.assumptions: The provider exposes an HTTPS endpoint that accepts a JSON payload, returns a 2xx response and supports one of Channel Builder's authentication methods. Administrators have the View custom channels and Manage custom channels permissions. Adobe locks the endpoint, headers, query parameters, authentication and payload structure once a channel is active, so every payload scenario is tested first. Changing throttling or retry settings on an active channel applies at once to all executions. Custom channels work in journeys, orchestrated campaigns and marketing campaigns, not in transactional campaigns.
services.exclusions: Provider-side setup and contracts, more than one channel, channel content production, and the native channels in JO01.
services.quote: To be able to use a custom channel in campaigns and journeys, an administrator must first create the channel. This involves defining the endpoint, authentication, throttling policy, and message payload structure. You can create the channel manually in the Channel Builder, as described below, or with the Channel Builder skill in Coworker.
services.why_distinct: JO01 sets up Journey Optimizer's native channels; no service prices a custom outbound channel.
services.review: Corrected in review: Adobe's own examples of services with no native channel, fields locked after activation, the API credentials, channel configuration and subdomain steps, and no transactional campaigns.

services.name: Email content production with Coworker's content skills
services.attach_to: [P15] Connection cw-ajo, under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Set up and pilot Coworker's Channel Content skills for your client's email work: check that the approved brand guidelines (voice, imagery and legal) are published where the Brand Lookup skill finds them, set up the reusable email design system Coworker maintains, store the Figma access token in Coworker's secrets and agree frame conventions for Build Email from Figma, define the brand, compliance, design and accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA) reviews each email passes, and agree how approved content is saved into Journey Optimizer templates. Pilot up to five emails from brief to saved draft and fix the template issues the reviews find.
services.deliverable: A content production guide, design system entries, a review checklist, up to five pilot emails saved as drafts, and the template fixes.
services.acceptance: Each pilot email passes the agreed reviews and saves into the right Journey Optimizer template or draft, and your client's content owner approves the guide.
services.assumptions: Templates and fragments exist (JO04). Images from a custom, brand-trained model need production access to Firefly Services (FM01 to FM05, XK08). Generated content is reviewed before it is saved.
services.exclusions: Template builds (JO04), content production after the pilot, Channel Content Create, custom model training and translation.
services.quote: Request all relevant reviews: Ask for brand, compliance, design, and accessibility review before treating content as send-ready.
services.why_distinct: JO04 builds templates and fragments by hand and XA26 writes journey Skills. Nothing prices setting up and piloting Coworker's content skills, the way AXD08 and AFX13 do for AEM pages and forms.
services.review: Kept in review. Step 86: the release label after Channel Content Create is gone (the tool check would fail on it); the exclusion stays.

services.name: Loyalty Challenges setup with Coworker
services.attach_to: [P16] Connection cw-ajo, under More services (default: false), with tier: Journey Optimizer Loyalty.
services.scope: Set up your client's Loyalty Challenges program so challenges can be built with Coworker: Loyalty roles (custom roles with Loyalty permissions in non-production sandboxes), the reward providers, event mappings, product inventory, exclusions and identity settings in Loyalty configurations, and the eligible audiences in Experience Platform. Build up to three first challenges with Coworker's Loyalty Challenge Management skill, write the challenge messages and content cards it does not fully automate, and review each challenge and its generated journey before publishing.
services.deliverable: The configured program, the role setup, up to three published challenges with their messages, and a prompt guide for future challenges.
services.acceptance: Test members complete each challenge's tasks and receive the reward through the configured provider, and the challenges report in the loyalty dashboards.
services.assumptions: Your client licenses Journey Optimizer Loyalty, which includes the loyalty skills even without a separate Coworker license. Reward fulfillment APIs and loyalty events are available from your client's loyalty platform.
services.exclusions: Loyalty platform changes, ingestion of loyalty data (RT02), Bring your own data challenges, more than three challenges and ongoing challenge operations.
services.quote: Before challenges can be authored, an administrator configures the program foundations: reward providers, event mappings that map customer actions to task completions, product inventory, and exclusion lists.
services.why_distinct: No service in the tool covers Loyalty Challenges, which Journey Optimizer made available on July 28, 2026 for organizations licensed for Journey Optimizer Loyalty (journey-optimizer/using/whats-new/previous-rn-new/release-notes-2026).
services.review: Kept in review. Step 86: Bring your own data challenges move from an availability sentence in the assumptions to the exclusions.

services.name: Target program audit and cleanup with Coworker
services.attach_to: [P17] Connection cw-target (Coworker and Target), under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Run Coworker's Target program audit and Recommendations checks on your client's account, then clean up what they find: resolve collisions and priority conflicts between activities, fix misconfigured activities, archive stale activities and remove the audiences and offers no activity uses, fix the feeds, catalog attributes and criteria behind empty or stale recommendations, and give Coworker your client's past test history as a CSV so its next-test advice draws on your client's own learnings.
services.deliverable: Audit findings before and after, the change log, the cleaned activity, audience and offer inventory, Recommendations fixes and the loaded test history.
services.acceptance: A rerun of the audit shows the agreed findings resolved, and your client's Target owner approves the remaining list.
services.assumptions: Users have Target roles that allow the changes. Changes to live activities are agreed with each activity owner first. Test history comes from your client's own records.
services.exclusions: New activities and the testing roadmap (TG03, TG05), Recommendations setup from scratch (TG04), Automated Personalization activities and implementation fixes (TG01).
services.quote: Audits Target programs for risks, collisions, misconfigurations, hygiene issues, and quick wins.
services.why_distinct: TG05 designs and analyzes new tests each month and XA27 writes Skills. No service cleans up an existing Target program from an audit.
services.review: Corrected in review: audiences and offers are removed once no activity uses them, since Target archives activities only.

services.name: Dispatcher, security and vulnerability fixes from Coworker findings
services.attach_to: [P18] Connection aemsites-cw (AEM Sites and Coworker), under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Use Coworker's Dispatcher Insights on your client's production and stage environments (a seven-day log window), with the Dispatcher configuration and related AEM code shared for review, and the Governance Agent's vulnerability list, to agree a prioritized fix list: cache rules and headers, filters and routing, redirects, security headers, permission-sensitive caching, CSRF and CORS settings, and affected components to patch or upgrade. Implement the agreed fixes in your client's code, deploy through Cloud Manager, and ask Coworker to reassess the logs or live URLs.
services.deliverable: Prioritized findings, the code and configuration changes, deployment records, before and after evidence from Coworker, and a list of items outside your client's control.
services.acceptance: The agreed fixes are live in production, Coworker's reassessment shows the targeted issues resolved, and your client's AEM owner approves the remaining list.
services.assumptions: Developers have Cloud Manager access to deploy and share the Dispatcher configuration and code, since Dispatcher Insights does not read or change the source repository, deploy, publish or clear caches. CDN cache purges, edge traffic filter rules and Adobe-managed settings are outside its scope.
services.exclusions: Site rebuilds, new features, CDN and traffic filter rule authoring, Adobe-managed infrastructure, and the runbook work in AXD09.
services.quote: After you apply and deploy a change, ask Coworker to reassess the available logs or live URL behavior.
services.why_distinct: AXD09 adds Dispatcher Insights to the runbook and SI04 validates Dispatcher at go-live. No service fixes what Coworker finds on a live site. The AEM release notes (experience-manager-cloud-service/content/release-notes/release-notes/release-notes-current) say Dispatcher Insights is generally available in Coworker Chat and add vulnerability assessment with the Governance Agent.
services.review: Kept as written.

services.name: Content Fragment readiness fixes with Coworker
services.attach_to: [P19] Connection aemsites-cw, under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Run Coworker's Content Fragment inspection on up to three of your client's fragment folders before a semantic search, translation, headless or publishing launch, then work through its human-reviewed remediation steps: fix the model, metadata, schema and reference issues, resolve risky dependencies before deletes, and agree the tags and review step for Coworker's bulk fragment edits. Rerun the checks until the folders pass.
services.deliverable: Readiness results before and after, the change log, dependency notes and the bulk edit rules.
services.acceptance: Each agreed folder passes the readiness checks for the planned launch, and your client's content owner approves the bulk edit rules.
services.assumptions: Your client uses Content Fragments on AEM as a Cloud Service and gives access to the models and folders. Model changes that affect live delivery are tested on a lower environment first.
services.exclusions: New fragment models or a content model redesign, migration, translation projects (SI08) and headless app development.
services.quote: Finally it provides assessments with guided, human-reviewed remediation steps.
services.why_distinct: No service fixes an existing fragment library; AXD10 creates fragments from Figma and XC05 models fragments for Journey Optimizer.
services.review: Kept as written.

services.name: Brand rules in Experience Context with a site audit
services.attach_to: [P20] Connection aemsites-cw, under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Build your client's Experience Context for one brand: gather the style guide, claim rules, positioning and design standards, import up to three brand policies from PDF or page URLs, review the rules and checks the Governance Agent extracts, add up to three segments (such as markets, audiences or sub-brands) over global defaults, enter the design system's colors and typography, map the domains and set everything to Active. Run a batch analysis of up to 50 existing pages, report aligned and non-aligned pages, and agree a fix plan and owners for rule updates.
services.deliverable: The populated Experience Context, the import review log, batch analysis results with a fix plan, and a rule ownership and update routine.
services.acceptance: Brand checks run on the agreed domain, your client's brand owner approves the rules and checks, and the batch analysis results are accepted as the baseline.
services.assumptions: Your client has AEM as a Cloud Service with the Governance Agent and supplies current brand documents and owners; documents already gathered for another Adobe product (such as BN01 or GS02) are reused. Only Active entities are used, and new ones start as Draft. Where A05 is also selected, it already configures the brand policy in the Governance Agent and validates checks on the agreed templates, so this service adds the segments, design system, domains and the batch site audit, and its hours are reduced.
services.exclusions: Fixing the non-aligned pages, writing new brand guidelines, more than one brand, the brand policy setup already priced in A05, the Skill brand context in CW-AEM and the context pack in CW02.
services.quote: New entities are created as Draft by default, so you must set an entity to Active to put it into effect.
services.why_distinct: A05 (on the Edge Delivery product and the AEM play) configures a brand policy in the Governance Agent and validates checks on templates, CW02 reviews one context pack and CW-AEM adds brand context to two Skills. No service on AEM Sites builds the full Experience Context (brands, rules with segments, design system, checks and domains) or audits an existing site against it with batch analysis. Coworker Chat uses it through the enterprise-context and aem-governance skills (coworker/content/chat/use-cases/workflows, Brand Governance).
services.review: Corrected in review: A05 already configures a brand policy, so that overlap is excluded and the hours drop when both are sold; brand documents gathered for BN01 or GS02 are reused.

services.name: Asset rights, Content Hub access rules and permission fixes
services.attach_to: [P21] Connection aemassets-cw (AEM Assets and Coworker), under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Use the AEM Governance Agent in Coworker to find your client's expired, expiring and undated assets in up to three folder trees, then add expiry dates and usage rights metadata to them in bulk in AEM Assets and set a review routine for assets about to expire. Design and create up to 10 Content Hub attribute-based access rules for groups, regions or agencies with the Governance Agent, written as ALLOW rules on IMS Group IDs and including a rule for each group that must see all assets, since Content Hub denies access to groups no rule covers. Apply the least-privilege group and ACL changes the Governance Agent recommends after diagnosing your client's repository permissions, since it does not change them itself.
services.deliverable: Rights metadata updates, the expiry review routine, the Content Hub access rules with test results, and the permission change log.
services.acceptance: Agreed assets carry expiry dates and rights metadata, test users see only the assets their rules allow in Content Hub, and the permission changes pass your client's access review.
services.assumptions: Your client has AEM Assets with the AEM agents, and Content Hub where access rules are needed, and supplies its rights terms and access policy. Access rules apply only to assets approved for Content Hub (Approval Target set to Content Hub) and need consistent metadata values such as brand and region. The rules are set up with AI Assistant in Content Hub, powered by the AEM Governance Agent. Coworker's permission diagnosis is read-only.
services.exclusions: Legal review of licenses, rights metadata beyond the agreed folders, Content Hub deployment (AS05) and user provisioning (AS01).
services.quote: The agentic capability is read-only: it diagnoses permissions and recommends changes, but it does not modify access control lists, groups, or content on your behalf.
services.why_distinct: AS07 and XG04 touch expiry only for published documents and for GenStudio's licensed assets, and A05 cites the same Governance Agent page for brand checks only. No service prices rights metadata across the DAM, Content Hub access rules or permission fixes, which the same Adobe page lists as Governance Agent capabilities. Rule guidelines (ALLOW rules only, IMS Group IDs, default deny, Approval Target set to Content Hub): experience-manager-cloud-service/content/assets/content-hub/attribute-based-access-control.
services.review: Corrected in review: Content Hub's ALLOW-only, default-deny rules on IMS Group IDs, assets approved for Content Hub, and expiry dates set in AEM Assets by people. Step 86: the condition on Adobe enabling the agent and the Adobe documents framing are gone; the license line already names the AEM agents.

services.name: Monthly Fusion scenario support through Coworker
services.attach_to: [P22] Connection workfront-cw (Workfront and Coworker), under More services (default: false), with ext: Workfront Fusion, as on XB16.
services.scope: Have your client's Fusion administrator turn on MCP access and decide who gets the write tools and which team roles, then each month use Coworker with Fusion to list failed and warning executions for up to 20 scenarios, explain the errors, check which scenarios depend on a connection, webhook or data store before changing it, fix the failing scenarios and expired connections, and report the month's failures, fixes and open risks.
services.deliverable: A monthly scenario health report with failures, fixes, dependency checks and open risks, and a record of who holds the write tools.
services.acceptance: Each month the agreed scenarios are reviewed, every failure has a fix or an owner, and destructive changes have your client's confirmation.
services.assumptions: Your client has Workfront Fusion and a Fusion organization, and Fusion is enabled in Coworker for it. Coworker acts with each user's Adobe ID, Fusion role and team roles, and Adobe says it is not responsible for changes the agent makes, so write tools stay with the named support users. After three months, review the volume with your client and resize the band.
services.exclusions: New scenario builds (XB16 and the other Fusion services), Fusion licenses, 24/7 support and the systems the scenarios connect to.
services.quote: Ask your Fusion administrator to enable write tools, or to grant you the required team role.
services.why_distinct: XB16 builds scenarios that call Coworker and WF06 covers Workfront administration. No service prices ongoing support of Fusion scenarios, which Coworker reads and explains through Fusion's built-in integration (fusion-mcp; tools listed at workfront-fusion/using/set-up-and-manage-fusion/use-fusion-mcp-server/fusion-mcp-server-tools).
services.review: Corrected in review: adds that Fusion is enabled in Coworker for the organization. Step 86: Adobe's industry note is out of the assumptions, since Adam's Nov 17 decision keeps it on the Workfront + Coworker card only (the tool check would fail on it here).

services.name: Organizational Rules for Coworker in Marketo Engage
services.attach_to: [P23] Connection marketo-cw (Marketo Engage and Coworker), under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Write your client's Organizational Rules for Coworker in Marketo Engage, starting from Adobe's defaults: naming patterns for programs, emails and Smart Campaigns, required folders, tokens and reports, and compliance rules such as unsubscribe links, footer details, UTM parameters and exclusion filters. Set the global rules and up to three workspace overrides, version them, test them with Validate Programs on real programs, and tune rules that block good programs.
services.deliverable: The Organizational Rules document with its version history, the workspace overrides, Validate Programs test results and a change note for the marketing operations team.
services.acceptance: Validate Programs applies your client's rules to the test programs as agreed, and your client's marketing operations owner approves the rules.
services.assumptions: Coworker for Marketo Engage is enabled and its access is set up (XB10). An administrator edits the rules. Smart List filters, flow steps, rendering, brand tone and dynamic content stay manual review steps.
services.exclusions: Building programs, fixing existing programs that fail the rules, and program templates (MK03).
services.quote: Every Marketo Engage environment includes default Organizational Rules. You can customize them to reflect your organization’s specific governance needs.
services.why_distinct: XB10 sets up access and pilots the skills on your client's templates. No service writes the rules that Build Programs, Plan Campaigns and Validate Programs all follow (workspace rules override global ones: marketo/using/product-docs/coworker-for-marketo/settings-setup).
services.review: Kept as written.

services.name: Monthly program builds with Coworker in Marketo Engage
services.attach_to: [P24] Connection marketo-cw, under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Each month, turn up to four of your client's campaign briefs into Marketo Engage programs with Coworker: plan each with Plan Campaigns, build it from the right template with Build Programs, then finish what stays manual (Smart List filters for the real segments, flow steps, placeholder emails and dynamic content), run the manual checks Coworker flags and Validate Programs against your client's rules, and activate after approval.
services.deliverable: Up to four launched programs a month, each with its plan, validation result and manual check record.
services.acceptance: Each program passes Validate Programs and the manual checks and is activated with your client's approval.
services.assumptions: Templates exist with at least one email and one Smart Campaign (MK03), and Organizational Rules are set (P23 or Adobe's defaults). Your client supplies the briefs, approved copy and target segments. After three months, review the volume with your client and resize the band.
services.exclusions: New templates, email design, instance administration (MK06), lead data fixes and programs beyond the monthly count.
services.quote: Email content is auto-generated, but Smart Campaign filters and flow steps remain manual.
services.why_distinct: MK03 builds templates and MK06 reviews the instance. No service prices ongoing program production, where Coworker builds the structure and people finish the filters and flow steps; Plan Campaigns does not create anything in Marketo Engage (marketo/using/product-docs/coworker-for-marketo/skills/plan-campaigns).
services.review: Kept as written.

services.name: Personas, intent model and AI decisioning data gaps
services.attach_to: [P25] Connection moptimizer-cw (Marketo Optimizer and Coworker), under More services (default: false).
services.scope: Prepare the data Marketo Optimizer's AI decisioning reads: define up to 10 personas from your client's person attributes in the persona mapping panel, set and activate the intent model's activity weights with Coworker's Intent configuration skill and check the results with Analyze intent, then use AI-decisioning health to find coverage gaps across demographic, firmographic, technographic, psychographic, persona and intent data and agree an enrichment plan for them.
services.deliverable: Persona definitions, the active intent model and its weights, AI-decisioning health reports before and after, and the enrichment plan.
services.acceptance: Persona classification improves against the first AI-decisioning health report, the approved intent model is active, and your client's marketing operations owner approves the personas, the weights and the enrichment plan.
services.assumptions: Marketo Optimizer is set up with data flowing from Marketo Engage. Persona mapping supports up to 20 personas, five attributes each and ten attributes in total. Only one intent model is active at a time. Intent reports need the View B2B Intent Reports permission. Enrichment vendors and data loads are priced separately, so coverage gains from enrichment come after this service.
services.exclusions: Engagement score weighting and people lists (MO04), next best path and journey traffic control (MO07), Scoring Studio and third-party data purchases.
services.quote: Closing those gaps improves how AI decisioning scores and routes each person.
services.why_distinct: MO04 uses the derived persona and engagement score as filters and MO07 runs AI path decisions. No service defines the personas, sets the intent model or closes the data gaps those decisions depend on (marketo-optimizer/user/coworker/intent; marketo-optimizer/user/admin/persona-mapping).
services.review: Corrected in review: acceptance now checks persona classification, the active model and the approvals, and the View B2B Intent Reports permission is added. Step 86: the release label after Scoring Studio is gone; the exclusion stays.

services.name: Webinar programs with Coworker in Marketo Optimizer
services.attach_to: [P26] Connection moptimizer-cw, under More services (default: false), with tier: Marketo Optimizer webinar license.
services.scope: Set up your client's first interactive webinar with Coworker: create the webinar in its program at the licensed capacity, design the registration page and room in the Adobe Connect design surface, build the promotion and post-webinar journeys Coworker drafts, finish what it lists as left to configure (the journey audience, the invitation email, the registration form event filter and the member status steps), test and publish, and leave a reusable webinar program for later events.
services.deliverable: One live webinar with its promotion and follow-up journeys, a tested registration path, and a reusable program with a prompt guide.
services.acceptance: Test registrants receive the invitation and joining link, attendance statuses update after the session, and the follow-up journey sends the right email to attendees and no-shows.
services.assumptions: Your client has the Marketo Optimizer webinar license and its additional terms. Delivery runs on Adobe Connect. Your client supplies the content, speakers and approved emails.
services.exclusions: Running or hosting the live session, video production, more than one webinar, other person journeys (MO05), and reporting beyond the engagement dashboard.
services.quote: The chat interface lists what is left to configure in the journey canvas.
services.why_distinct: MK03 builds webinar program templates in Marketo Engage. No service sets up Marketo Optimizer's interactive webinars, which Coworker drafts while the room design and journey details are left to people.
services.review: Corrected in review: other person journeys (MO05) are excluded so they are not charged twice.
